CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  NOTICE OF REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE
  ALHAMBRA TRANSPORTATION COMMISSION
  WEDNESDAY, JULY 13, 2022
  7:00 p.m.

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a Regular Meeting of the Alhambra
Transportation Commission will be held on Wednesday, July 13, 2022 at
7:00 p.m. pursuant to the order of the Alhambra Transportation Commission
Secretary.

Consistent with AB 361, the Alhambra Transportation Commission
meeting will not be physically open to the public, although the public
may participate by video conference or teleconference and some of the
Commission Members may choose to participate via video conference
or teleconference.

An agenda of such regular meeting is attached hereto, incorporated herein by
reference and made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.

  Martin W. Ray
  Alhambra Transportation Commission Secretary

Notice No: N2M22-83
Posted:  July 7, 2022
   CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  AGENDA
  TRANSPORTATION COMMISSION
  July 13, 2022
  MISSION STATEMENT
  The City of Alhambra is dedicated to responsive, creative leadership and quality
  services, ensuring desirable neighborhoods and a supportive business
  environment, while being sensitive to the diversity of our community.

  CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19) ADVISORY NOTICE
Consistent with AB 361, the Alhambra Transportation Commission meeting will not be physically open
to the public, although the public may participate by video conference or teleconference and some
of the Council Members may choose to participate via video conference or teleconference rather
than attend in person.

To watch and listen to the meeting: To maximize public safety while still maintaining transparency and
public access, members of the public can participate by using Zoom Webinar as follows:

Zoom Webinar direct link:
https://cityofalhambra-org.zoom.us/j/84338295183?pwd=MUdpcjljNFFNVDJkQmhaVUFNcmNIQT09

Meeting ID: 843 3829 5183, Passcode: 321319

Or by telephone by dialing 888-475-4499 (Toll Free) or 833-548-0276 (Toll Free) or 833-548-0282 (Toll
Free) or 877-853-5257 (Toll Free) or 1-669-900-9128 or 1-346-248-7799 or 1-253-215-8782 or 1-646-558-
8656 or 1-301-715-8592 or 1-312-626-6799 and entering Meeting ID: 843 3829 5183, Passcode:
321319. Please Note: All members of the public calling or logging into the meeting will be muted so that
the meeting can proceed.

Addressing the Transportation Commission

Via Zoom or Telephone: “Raise your hand” - Members of the public may speak by using the “Raise Hand”
function during the public comments portion, if on Zoom or telephone. Staff will unmute speakers
participating via Zoom or telephone and announce your name when it is your time to speak.

Remarks are limited to 5 minutes; however, the presiding officer may either extend or reduce the
maximum time to such period of time as the Commission may determine.

  PRESENTATIONS

  1. ELECTION OF OFFICERS

  Each year the committee is appointed by the City Council. At this time, it is appropriate to conduct
  an election to determine which members will chair the meeting as president and in the event the
  chair cannot attend the meeting, determine which member will step in as Vice President to
  conduct the meeting.

  Recommended Action: That the Committee elect a new president and vice president to chair the
  meeting.

  2.  TRAFFIC REVIEW OF REQUEST FOR RED CURB ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF DRIVEWAY
  AT 928 S 2ND STREET TO INCREASE LINE OF SIGHT AT THE DRIVEWAY

  Staff will review the report that was prepared in response to a concern of resident having difficulty
  when larger vehicles or vehicles park too close to their driveway limiting their ability to safely enter
  and exit the driveway especially when backing out.

  After a thorough review of existing field and traffic conditions and per the guidelines in the
  California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (CAMUTCD), California Vehicle Code
  (CVC), and based on engineering judgement, a list of options is presented to Traffic Commission
  for review and direction.

  Recommended Action

  It is recommended that the Transportation Commission review the report with the City Traffic
  Engineer, listen to public comment and provide direction.

 3. TRAFFIC REVIEW OF REQUEST FOR RED CURB ON RED CURB ON CONCORD
  AVENUE FOR RESIDENCE AT 648 SOUTH MERIDIAN AVENUE

Staff will review the report that was prepared in response to a concern of resident having difficulty
exiting their driveway due to poor line-of-sight from parked cars on the north side of Concord
Avenue. The resident also stated that residents living on the south side of Concord Avenue
park their vehicles on the north side of Concord Avenue, adding to the line-of-sight issue.

After a thorough review of existing field and traffic conditions and per the guidelines in the
California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (CAMUTCD), California Vehicle Code
(CVC), and based on engineering judgement, a list of options is presented to Traffic Commission
for review and direction.

Recommended Action

It is recommended that the Transportation Commission review the report with the City Traffic
Engineer, listen to public comment and provide direction.

4. PUBLIC COMMENTS

Comments must pertain to the business of the Transportation Commission. Kindly limit all oral
communications to five (5) minutes.

5. COMMENTS AND CONCERNS FROM COMMISSION MEMBERS AND/OR STAFF.

Comments, concerns or discussion on any item(s) not specified on the agenda. Items discussed
must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Transportation Commission.

6. ADJOURNMENT

  Adjournment to a regular meeting on Wednesday, September 14, 2022 at 7:00 p.m.

Copies of staff reports or other written documentation, if any, relating to each item of business
described above are on file in the Alhambra City Hall, Public Works Department, 111 S. First
Street, Alhambra California 91801 and are available for public inspection upon request during
regular business hours of 7:00am to 5:30pm, Monday through Thursday.

Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the
meeting described herein, he or she may contact Martin Ray, Director of Public Works & Utilities,
either in person at the Public Works Department at Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, or
by calling via telephone at (626) 570-5067 during regular business hours.

DATE:  May 4, 2022
SUBJECT:  TRAFFIC REVIEW OF REQUEST FOR RED CURB ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF DRIVEWAY AT 928
  S 2ND STREET TO INCREASE LINE OF SIGHT AT THE DRIVEWAY

INTRODUCTION

The City of Alhambra received a request for red curb to be installed to the south of a resident’s driveway
at 928 S 2nd Street. The applicant is requesting that either red tips or full red curb be installed to the south
of his driveway. The resident has complained that when larger vehicles or vehicles park too close to the
driveway it limits the ability to safely enter and exit the driveway especially when backing out. In response
to this request and on behalf of the City, engineering staff has completed a traffic review to evaluate
existing conditions along the curb to the south of the driveway. The traffic review included an analysis of
existing roadway conditions as well as a thorough review of the CMUTCD (California Manual on Uniform
Traffic Control Devices) and CVC (California Vehicle Code).

South 2nd Street - Within the City of Alhambra, South 2nd Street runs north and south and is considered a
local road per the California Road Systems Map by Caltrans. South 2nd Street has a prima facie speed limit
of 25 MPH and is approximately 35 feet wide with one lane in each direction, and no marked centerline.
This section of S 2nd Street is a long stretch with STOP control at Palmetto Drive to the north and San
Marino Avenue to the south (1600’). Parking is permitted on both sides of the street where there are no
red curbs marked or restricted by signage. Parking is not permitted on Wednesdays from Noon to 3 PM
due to street sweeping, parking is also not permitted without a City Permit from 2 AM to 6 AM on all
streets. The section of South 2nd Street lies within a Low-Density Residential zone per the Alhambra Zoning
Map.

EXISTING FIELD CONDITIONS

A review was undertaken to look at existing curb conditions in the field. Presently, the 928 S 2nd Street
driveway is about 8’ wide with driveway aprons of 11.8’. There is available parking of 20.4’ for one vehicle
directly to the south of the driveway and then 20’ of red curb to the NE corner of Linda Vista Avenue (Exh
A). At the time of the field visit there was a large pick-up parked in the space with its bumper extending
into the red curb. To have a clear view of approaching vehicles heading NB a backing vehicle needs to
hover around the sidewalk (10’ -12’ back from curb) to see around a parked vehicle or proceed to back
out by inching until the driver can see around a parked car but this would put the rear of the vehicle in
the travel way. It seems that this seems to be the case all along the entire block of S 2nd Street. The house
directly to the south of the residence has a doorway and walkway on S 2nd Street as well as on Linda Vista

the north side there is 25.5’ of red curb and then 80’ of regular parking from the red to the next driveway
(Exh B). The 80’ would allow for 4 vehicles to park assuming a 20 foot parking space.

RECOMMENDATIONS

After a thorough review of existing field and traffic conditions and per the guidelines in the California
Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (CAMUTCD), California Vehicle Code (CVC), and based on
engineering judgement, a list of options is presented to Traffic Commission for review and direction.
Please refer to the figures below for a conceptual exhibit of the proposed recommendations.

  •  OPTION 1: DENY THE REQUEST SINCE THIS IS THE CONDITION ALL ALONG S 2ND STREET

  •  OPTION 2: INSTALL 3-FEET OF NEW RED CURB ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF THE DRIVEWAY: Install 3-
  feet of red curb on the south side of the driveway. This will allow for a smaller car to still park with
  17-feet of available parking. Visibility for backing drivers may be improved by looking over a
  regular size vehicle.

  •  OPTION 3: INSTALL 20-FEET OF NEW RED CURB: Install 20-feet of new red curb to the south of
  the 928 South 2nd Street driveway connecting to the existing red curb north of W Linda Vista
  Avenue. This will remove one parking spot and will provide for a clear line of sight for backing
  vehicles. 80-feet of parking is available on W Linda Vista Avenue for the house on the corner.

DATE:  June 24, 2022
SUBJECT:  RED CURB REQUEST ON CONCORD AVENUE FOR RESIDENCE AT 648 SOUTH MERIDIAN
  AVENUE

INTRODUCTION

The City of Alhambra received a resident request for red curb to be installed to the east of the applicant’s
648 South Meridian Avenue driveway which is located along Concord Avenue. The resident expressed that
they were having difficulty exiting their driveway due to poor line-of-sight from parked cars on the north
side of Concord Avenue. The resident also stated that residents living on the south side of Concord Avenue
park their vehicles on the north side of Concord Avenue, adding to the line-of-sight issue. In response to
this request and on behalf of the City, engineering staff has completed a traffic review to evaluate existing
conditions along Concord Avenue to the east of the residents’ address of 648 South Meridian Avenue. The
traffic review included an analysis of existing roadway conditions as well as a thorough review of the
CMUTCD (California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices) and CVC (California Vehicle Code).

Concord Avenue - Within the City of Alhambra, Concord Avenue runs northeast and southwest and is
considered a Minor Arterial per the California Road Systems Map by Caltrans. Concord Avenue has a
posted speed limit of 25 MPH and is approximately 40-feet wide with one lane in each direction, and a
yellow dashed centerline. Parking is permitted on both sides of the street where there are no red curbs
painted or restricted by signage. Parking is not permitted on either side of Concord Avenue on Thursdays
between 8AM to 11 AM due to street sweeping. This section of Concord Avenue is within a Low-Density
Residential zone per the Alhambra Zoning Map.

RECOMMENDATIONS

After a thorough review of existing field and traffic conditions and per the guidelines in the California
Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (CAMUTCD), California Vehicle Code (CVC), and based on
engineering judgement, there are two options that are presented to Traffic Commission for review and
direction. Please refer to the figures below for a conceptual exhibit of the proposed recommendations.

  •  OPTION 1: LEAVE EXISTING CONDITIONS AS IS: No red curb to be added to Concord Avenue. This
  condition exists for similar driveways on Concord Avenue.

  •  OPTION 2: INSTALL 20-FEET OF RED CURB: Extend the existing red curb 20-feet on the north side
  of Concord Avenue on the east side of the driveway. This will remove one parking spot and will
  provide for a clear line of sight for backing vehicles.
